tickets.subject: Generation stalls at ~60% with Anthropic provider
tickets.body: Running QBORT 0.1.0 on macOS 15.3, targeting 200 tickets against Claude via Anthropic. The run gets to roughly 120 tickets and the progress bar just freezes — no error dialog, but the last batch never resolves. Console shows "fetch failed: ETIMEDOUT" a couple times. I've retried twice with the same stall point. Any way to make batches retry automatically, or is my key rate-limited?

responses.body: Thanks for the detail, Marcus. The ETIMEDOUT points at a transient network/rate-limit issue mid-batch rather than a bad key. In 0.1.0 a stalled batch won't auto-retry, so the run parks. Lower the concurrency in settings (try 2 batches) and reduce batch size — that usually clears the rate ceiling. We're tracking automatic per-batch retry for the next release.

tickets.subject: "App is damaged and can't be opened" on first launch
tickets.body: Just downloaded the QBORT 0.1.0 zip from the GitHub release and macOS 15.2 throws "QBORT is damaged and can't be opened. You should move it to the Trash." I know it's unsigned, but the usual right-click > Open trick isn't even offered. What's the correct way to get past Gatekeeper here?

responses.body: That message is Gatekeeper quarantining the unsigned build after download. Run `xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/QBORT.app` in Terminal (adjust the path to wherever you moved it), then launch normally. The right-click > Open path is suppressed once the "damaged" flag is set, which is why you didn't see it. That should clear it — let us know if it persists.

tickets.subject: Add CSV export alongside tickets.json
tickets.body: We love the JSON output, but our helpdesk import tooling only ingests CSV. Right now I'm writing a little script to flatten tickets.json into rows, but a native CSV export (one row per message, or per ticket with a messages column) would save the whole team a step. Is that on the roadmap?

responses.body: Appreciate the request, Tomás — CSV export has come up a few times and it's a natural fit next to the JSON exporter. Quick question so we scope it right: would you prefer one row per ticket (with messages serialized into a column) or one row per message with a shared ticket id? Your flattening script suggests the latter.
One row per message with a ticket id is exactly what we'd want — that maps cleanly onto our importer. Thanks for considering it.

tickets.subject: Exported JSON malformed after large Ollama run
tickets.body: On QBORT 0.1.0 (macOS 14.7) I ran 500 tickets through a local Ollama llama3.1 model. The run reported success, but when I open the exported tickets.json my parser chokes with "Unexpected end of JSON input". Looks truncated near the end. Smaller runs (50) export fine. Is the file getting written before generation finishes?

responses.body: Thanks Hannah — truncation on the large run but not the small one is a useful clue. QBORT writes tickets.json atomically (temp file + rename), so a partial file usually means the write was interrupted rather than a normal flush. Can you confirm whether the app was still showing an active run when you opened the file, or had it fully returned to the idle state?
It had returned to idle and showed "500 tickets" in the panel. I opened the file a few seconds later. The app didn't crash.

Got it. If the panel counted 500 and it still truncated, that points at the coalesced write for the final batch dropping content rather than a mid-run interruption. Could you check the file size and whether it ends inside a ticket object (mid-string) versus at a clean array boundary? That tells us if it's a serialization cutoff vs. an encoding issue.
File is ~1.8 MB and it ends mid-string inside a "body" field — no closing braces or brackets. Definitely a cutoff, not clean.

That's what we needed. A mid-string cutoff on the final coalesced write is reproducible on our side at high ticket counts with local models that stream slowly. I'm filing this as a bug — the fix is to fully buffer the last batch before the atomic rename. As a workaround, splitting the run into two 250-ticket passes and merging avoids the truncation entirely.
Confirmed — two 250 passes both exported valid JSON. Thanks for digging in, I'll use that until the fix ships.

tickets.subject: How does the staff-response distribution actually work?
tickets.body: The docs mention a target for staff responses per ticket but I can't find where it explains the distribution. If I set responses on, do all tickets get the same number of replies, or is it spread somehow? Trying to model a realistic mix for a demo dataset and want to understand what QBORT is doing under the hood before I tune it.

responses.body: Good question, Devin — it's a spread, not a flat count. QBORT distributes replies around your target so some tickets get zero and others get several, approximating a real inbox rather than a uniform thread length. Setting the target to, say, 2 gives you a realistic mix centered near two replies. We'll get this written up more clearly in the docs since it's not obvious today.
